steps.speaker: fenwick
steps.text: The far bank at last. I'd begun to think that ford went on forever.

steps.speaker: elara
steps.text: There is a house off the road ahead. I have sheltered there before. It has sound walls, and a well that still draws clean water.

steps.speaker: player
steps.text: This place is in finer shape than I expected. It is a shame to see it stand abandoned.

steps.speaker: fenwick
steps.text: Why would a body walk away from a place like this? Sound walls, sweet well. Someone kept it well for years.

steps.speaker: elara
steps.text: A house is only worth its neighbors. When the road empties, the last family on it does not stay long — no smith, no market, no one to send for when the fever takes a child. Sound walls will not feed anyone alone.

steps.speaker: fenwick
steps.text: It feels wrong, bedding down in a dead family's house.

steps.speaker: player
steps.text: They're not dead. They're only gone. And a roof's a roof — we'll not find a better one before dark.

steps.speaker: fenwick
steps.text: ...No sense letting a good hearth sit cold, I suppose.
